newsitem.title: UK: Regulator slams low Railtrack investment.
newsitem.headline: Regulator slams low Railtrack investment.

text.p: The maintenance record of British rail infrastructure operator Railtrack Group Plc has been criticised by the main railway industry regulator, the Office of the Rail Regulator (ORR), in a letter made public on Friday.

Regulator John Swift wrote in response to a complaint by lobby group Save Our Railways that he agreed Railtrack was not making sufficient progressing in renewing the national rail network over time "in modern equivalent form".
"The current level of underspend is wholly unacceptable to me and I expect prompt action to remedy this," Swift said, adding he felt the company was being slow to accelerate spending.

The discussion about maintenance and investment standards is currently being carried out across the industry, including in consultations with Railtrack, ahead of Railtrack's planned publication in February next year of its annual planning document, called its Network Management Statement (NMS).

In a clear indication of how he has contributed to this debate, Swift said, "When Railtrack publishes its NMS in February I expect it to demonstrate, publicly, its commitment and capability to deliver an infrastructure investment programme which meets the objectives I have set out above".
He also said he would set new regulatory targets next year.
